notes: OFFICIAL WINDOW OPENED 2026-09-01 (Asia/Tokyo). Official revenue ¥0, official cost small (see cost_ledger.json). TWO corrections applied honestly this same day. (1) 2026-09-01T15:30 UTC: an inventory at 14:30 UTC had wrongly treated 'no GitHub repo record' for Gumroad/Creem as evidence those accounts were never opened. Owner corrected directly: both accounts are open with KYC/bank done (Gumroad fully ready, Creem last known under review) -- a gap in what got migrated to GitHub memory, not in what the owner did. Introduced an explicit verification-level taxonomy (confirmed_in_repo | confirmed_by_owner | status_unknown | needs_re_verification). (2) 2026-09-01T16:30 UTC: the Gumroad pipeline built in response to (1) had trusted antiwork/gumroad-cli's own documentation as evidence its product-publish commands work, without checking Gumroad's official help center (which only documents that CLI for Pages/Profile publishing) or the actual API behavior. Owner flagged this correctly, including the risk of confusing it with an unrelated third-party 'GumroadPro CLI.' Re-verified from Gumroad's actual production Rails source directly (github.com/antiwork/gumroad: routes.rb + api/v2 controllers) rather than the CLI's docs or WebSearch summaries -- one of which had separately, and per the source incorrectly, claimed the create-product endpoint 404s. Confirmed POST /v2/products (create), the ActiveStorage direct-upload file flow, and PUT .../enable (publish) are real, working, unguarded routes requiring only the edit_products OAuth scope. Rebuilt scripts/gumroad_publish.mjs to call the REST API directly -- no CLI dependency, first- or third-party -- and switched the owner's grant to Gumroad's simpler personal-access-token path (Settings -> Advanced, ops/GUMROAD_API_SETUP.md) instead of the CLI's device-flow login. Two implementation details (direct_uploads response field names; files-array entry shape) remain honestly flagged as unverified against a live call, not presented as certain. Strategic conclusion held throughout both corrections: Gumroad's grant is simpler than Etsy's and worth activating in parallel, now verified against primary source rather than secondary documentation. Creem stays deliberately un-built (duplicates Stripe's role, no distribution advantage identified) regardless of confirmed account/KYC. Nothing has been published or sold on Gumroad yet -- reported honestly. (3) 2026-09-01T17:00 UTC: owner asked to re-check, specifically for Gumroad, whether Browser/Computer-Use publishing should be tried before the REST API path -- not assuming the earlier Etsy finding carries over. Investigated fresh with live tests: no browser-driving tool in this session (re-searched), and a direct connectivity test shows gumroad.com/app.gumroad.com/gumroad.com/login are ALL blocked at the sandbox egress proxy (whole-domain, confirmed live, not reused from the Etsy check). Confirms the REST API pipeline as necessary, not merely convenient -- no code changes needed since it already exists; recorded the investigation. Full timeline: status/EVENTS.jsonl and ops/AGENT_LOOP.md. (4) 2026-09-02T22:00-22:17 UTC: owner registered GUMROAD_ACCESS_TOKEN and asked for a real, live end-to-end publish (not just capability-building). 1st run's real error (400 on /v2/direct_uploads: 'content_type must be JPEG, PNG, GIF, or video') showed the previously-flagged-uncertain file-upload path was actually wrong, not merely unverified -- that endpoint is media-only. Read files_controller.rb directly, found the correct S3-multipart /v2/files/presign -> /v2/files/complete flow, applied a minimal fix, re-ran, succeeded. Gumroad listing is now live and purchasable at https://feverish50.gumroad.com/l/uhajxo ($9) -- reported honestly as 'listing published', explicitly distinct from 'first sale' (which has not happened). Etsy OAuth grant is now the sole remaining blocker.
